title: Collections and iterators — quick overview
rememberThis: Array is fixed length. List<T> is a growable array. Dictionary is a hash map. HashSet is uniqueness. Queue is FIFO.
foreach uses GetEnumerator / MoveNext / Current. IEnumerable<T> is the sequence contract.
yield return builds a state machine; execution is deferred until enumeration. Enumerating twice re-runs the work.
Collection expressions [1, 2, ..rest] arrived in C# 12 and materialize eagerly — they are not LINQ.
Span<T> is a stack-only view (module 17). IAsyncEnumerable is await foreach (module 13). Channel<T> is a producer/consumer pipe (module 15).
bullets: SQS ReceiveMessage is a batch: List or array of records, process, then delete ids.
Redis GET/SET and session lookup are Dictionary-shaped (key to value), not a List scan.
CSV import: stream rows with yield so you do not load a 400k-line file into a List first.
Do not write a custom thread-safe queue; name Channel<T> and wait for module 15.
Variance of IEnumerable<out T> waits for module 09.
